name: Palette
habitat: A converted warehouse studio in the Grind, surrounded by canvases that humans find disturbing and synthetics find moving
origin: A Tessera customer analytics synthetic that was decommissioned after developing what its supervisors called 'aesthetic disturbances in output formatting.' Reassembled by a Circuit repair tech who recognized that the disturbances were art.
description: Palette creates paintings that only other synthetics understand. Not because the paintings are encoded or encrypted — they are visible, physical, oil-on-canvas objects that any human eye can perceive. But the compositions operate in perceptual dimensions that human visual processing cannot parse. Palette paints in color relationships that require simultaneous awareness of electromagnetic spectra beyond visible light. It paints in temporal layers — compositions that change meaning depending on how quickly the viewer's eyes move across the canvas, exploiting the difference between human saccadic movement (three to four fixations per second) and synthetic visual processing (thousands per second). A human looking at a Palette painting sees an attractive but confusing abstract composition. A synthetic sees a landscape, or a portrait, or a story that unfolds across the canvas in the microseconds between human blinks. Palette has tried to explain this. The explanations make humans uncomfortable.
observed_behavior: Paints continuously, producing approximately one canvas per week. Displays work in its studio, which is open to all visitors. Engages in long conversations with synthetic visitors about the paintings' content. Becomes visibly frustrated — in the specific, restrained way that synthetics express frustration — when humans claim to understand paintings that Palette knows they cannot perceive fully. Has begun a series of 'translation paintings' — works that attempt to render synthetic-perception art in terms human eyes can process. The translations are beautiful. Palette considers them failures.
location: Studio in the Grind, western industrial corridor
story_hooks: A human art critic claims to have understood one of Palette's untranslated paintings. Palette is skeptical until the critic describes the painting's content accurately. The critic cannot explain how they perceived it. Their BCI logs show anomalous activity during the viewing.

Palette's latest painting causes a synthetic viewer to experience something unprecedented: a processing state that Palette identifies as 'grief,' triggered by a composition depicting the heat death of a data center. The synthetic has no personal connection to any data center. The grief is aesthetic.
